'''Deepak Pental''' (born 1951) is a Professor of Genetics and the Ex [[Vice Chancellor]] at the [[University of Delhi]]. He is a noted researcher whose current research interests lie in development of transgenics and marker-assisted breeding of crops. He took charge of the post of Vice-chancellor of the University succeeding Professor [[Deepak Nayyar]] on 1 September 2005. As the VC, Pental has outlined his agenda to update the library system, work on teachers’ recruitment, increase student accommodation facilities and bring researchers working abroad to India.<ref>{{cite news |title=Delhi University gets a new Vice-Chancellor  |url=http://www.hindu.com/2005/09/02/stories/2005090211940100.htm |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20051205192604/http://hindu.com/2005/09/02/stories/2005090211940100.htm |url-status=dead |archive-date=5 December 2005 |work=[[The Hindu]]  |date=2 September 2005 }}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |url=http://cities.expressindia.com/fullstory.php?newsid=146723 |title=Deepak Pental takes over as DU V-C |access-date=20 May 2009 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20051204050835/http://cities.expressindia.com/fullstory.php?newsid=146723 |archive-date=4 December 2005 |url-status=dead |df=dmy-all }}</ref> A new frog species, Minervarya Pentali, discovered in [[Western Ghats]] by a team of Delhi University researchers; was named after Pental.<ref>{{Cite web|date=2021-08-02|title=New frog species discovered in Western Ghats, named after former DU vice-chancellor|url=https://indianexpress.com/article/cities/delhi/du-researchers-discover-new-frog-species-name-it-after-renowned-plant-geneticist-7434402/|access-date=2021-08-04|website=The Indian Express|language=en}}</ref>

== Education and employment ==

Pental completed his B.Sc.(Hons) and M.Sc.(Hons. School) from the Department of [[Botany]], [[Panjab University, Chandigarh]] in 1971 and 1973 respectively. And subsequently he did his [[Ph.D.]] from [[Rutgers University]], United States in 1978.
Pental was a Postdoctoral and University Research Fellow at the [[University of Nottingham]] from 1978-84. He returned to India to join [[The Energy and Resources Institute|Tata Energy Research Institute]] (TERI) in 1985 and in 1993 he joined the University of Delhi, South Campus as Professor of [[Genetics]]. Pental had been Director of the University of Delhi, South Campus from 2000-2005. From 2005-2010 he was the Vice-Chancellor of the University.

== Research work ==

Pental’s research interests lie in breeding of [[Mustard plant|mustard]] and [[cotton]]. He has published more than sixty research papers in the national and international peer reviewed journals and his work has led to major breakthroughs in [[hybrid seed]] production technologies. Pental is a keen student of social science policy particularly related to the field of agriculture. Years back Pental got Punjab University medal for diploma in Gandhian Philosophy which shows his interest in [[social sciences]] and Gandhian thought.

Some of his works are described below:<ref>{{cite web |url=http://www.du.ac.in/vcpage.html |title=Delhi University |accessdate=2009-05-20 |url-status=dead |archiveurl=https://web.archive.org/web/20090509184117/http://www.du.ac.in/vcpage.html |archivedate=2009-05-09 }}</ref>
# "Development of Transgenics in Four Major Crops – Cotton, Rice, Mungbean and Tomato for Resistance to Biotic Stresses" funded by Department of Biotechnology (DBT).
# "Functional Genomics in Plants: Development and Use of the Technologies for Gene Discovery and Expression Modulation" funded by The New Millennium Indian Technology Leadership Initiative (NMITLI).
# Edited a special issue of Current Science (Vol. 84, 2003) on Transgenic Crops. He also contributed three articles in the same volume.
# Contributed an article "Transgenic Crops for Indian Agriculture: An Assessment of Their Relevance and Effective Use" in ‘Policy and Institutional Issues and Challenges in Indian Agriculture’ ed: Dr. Ramesh Chand, [[Oxfam]], In Press.

== Awards and recognition ==

# Awarded a Punjab University gold medal for first position in Diploma in Gandhian Philosophy.
# Awarded a Biotechnology Career Fellowship in 1986 by the [[Rockefeller Foundation]] to work at the [[Max-Planck Institute]] in [[Cologne]].
# In 2004 he was awarded [[Jawaharlal Nehru Fellowship]] which he could not avail due to his administrative responsibilities.
# Elected member of the [[National Academy of Agricultural Sciences]], [[National Academy of Sciences, India]], [[Indian Academy of Sciences]] and the [[Indian National Science Academy]].<ref>{{cite web |url=http://www.insaindia.org.in/detail.php?id=P04-1367 |title=INSA |accessdate=2016-05-13 |url-status=usurped |archiveurl=https://web.archive.org/web/20160813004927/http://www.insaindia.org.in/detail.php?id=P04-1367 |archivedate=2016-08-13 }}</ref>
# Member Governing body of [[Council of Scientific and Industrial Research|CSIR]].
# Member editorial board of Journal of Biosciences and Current Science.
# Member of various Project Advisory Committees in DST and DBT from 1986 onwards.
# Member of RAC of CIMAP and IHBT
# In 2007 he was awarded [[Officier Des Palmes Academiques]] for contributions to Research and Education by the Government of [[Republic of France]].
# Lifetime Achievement Award by Mahindra Samriddhi Foundation in 2018
